s: Job is upright and blessed. Satan says Job's faith depends on his good fortune, and Job loses his children and wealth, yet blesses God.
Job is struck with sores but will not curse God. Three friends come to comfort him.
Job curses the day he was born.
Eliphaz says the innocent do not perish, so Job must have sinned.
Eliphaz urges Job to turn to God and accept his correction.
Job says his grief is heavy and his friends have failed him.
Job laments that life is hard labour and asks God to leave him alone.
Bildad says God does not reject the blameless.
Job asks how a man can be just before God, who is so mighty.
Job wishes he had never been born and asks God why he afflicts him.
Zophar tells Job to repent so God will restore him.
Job answers that God's ways in the world are beyond human control.
Job wants to argue his case with God and calls his friends worthless physicians.
Job reflects that human life is short and full of trouble.
Eliphaz accuses Job of undermining the fear of God.
Job calls his friends miserable comforters and longs for a witness in heaven.
Job feels near death and without hope.
Bildad describes the fate of the wicked.
Job feels abandoned by all, but declares: I know that my Redeemer lives.
Zophar says the joy of the wicked is short-lived.
Job points out that the wicked often prosper in this life.
Eliphaz accuses Job of great sins and urges him to return to God.
Job longs to find God and present his case.
Job complains that God seems not to punish oppressors.
Bildad says no man can be pure before God.
Job praises God's power over creation.
Job holds fast to his innocence.
A poem on wisdom: hidden from all, it is the fear of the Lord.
Job remembers his former blessed days.
Job laments his present humiliation.
Job swears to his innocence in every area of life.
Young Elihu, angry with Job and his friends, begins to speak.
Elihu says God speaks to people through dreams and suffering.
Elihu defends God's justice.
Elihu says human sin or goodness cannot harm or help God.
Elihu says God uses suffering to teach, and praises his greatness.
Elihu describes God's majesty in the storm.
God answers Job out of the whirlwind: where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?
God asks Job about the wild animals that he alone cares for.
Job puts his hand over his mouth. God describes the mighty behemoth.
God describes Leviathan, whom no one can tame.
Job repents in dust and ashes. God rebukes the friends and restores Job twice over.

19: In the depths of his suffering, Job still hopes to see God. These words have comforted believers for centuries.
38: God does not explain Job's suffering but shows him his greatness and care for all creation. Job learns to trust.
